title: Diffusion Score Estimation with Shallow Neural Networks: Regularity, Approximation, and Finite-Sample Rates
abstract: arXiv:2610.27206v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: We study the sample complexity of estimating Ornstein--Uhlenbeck diffusion scores in $\mathbb R^d$ using denoising score matching (DSM) with finite-width shallow ReLU networks, and its implications for reverse-process sampling. Under weak differentiability and polynomial-growth conditions on normalized derivatives of the initial density, we combine complementary estimates from the Gaussian transition kernel and the initial density to obtain explicit Sobolev bounds that are uniform in time on each fixed ball. Combining these bounds with existing shallow-network approximation theory gives explicit control of the approximation error and a sufficient path-norm budget. We then use truncation and localized Rademacher complexity to establish high-probability risk bounds for path-norm-constrained empirical DSM minimizers with unbounded inputs and labels. tldr: 该论文为用浅层 ReLU 网络通过去噪分数匹配估计 Ornstein–Uhlenbeck 扩散分数建立了显式的有限样本理论，给出了时间一致的 Sobolev 正则性界、基于路徑范数的逼近误差控制，以及无界输入下经验 DSM 最小化器的高概率泛化风险界。
